interactions.summary: A student identifies the world's turn to Christianity as the key evidence, and Jiang expands that answer into a long argument that Christianity's conquest of billions is itself a miracle requiring divine explanation.
A Christian student says the dialectical challenge is not insulting but part of the journey, and Jiang accepts the point before continuing.

Another student asks why Dante would prove Christianity to an already Christian elite audience, and Jiang answers by contrasting Dante's imaginative inquiry with the anti-questioning reflex of a medieval priest.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Student question and Jiang answer setup

claims.claim: Jiang says the existence of roughly two billion Christians is itself a miracle because Christianity is conceptually confusing enough that its global success is difficult to explain on ordinary grounds.
He argues that unless one accepts a divine plan, the spread of Christianity is harder to explain than the rise of a hero cult around obvious conquerors like Caesar or Alexander.
Jiang presents Dante's procedure as revolutionary because it invites logical and imaginative questioning about faith rather than treating questioning itself as Satanic.
He says that in the year 1300 a priest would likely answer faith questions by accusing the questioner of speaking for Satan, which is why Dante staging such inquiry in heaven is so radical.

signature_moments.moment: Christianity's victory over the world is framed as the real miracle because the religion is so paradoxical and confusing on its face.
signature_moments.source_phrase: it's a miracle that this very confusing religion is able to conquer the world
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is Jiang's strongest modern restatement of Dante's conversion-of-the-world argument.

signature_moments.moment: Instead of letting the priest end the question with 'Satan is in you,' Dante makes heaven itself host a logical inquiry.
signature_moments.source_phrase: let's actually try to logically use our imagination
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It compresses Jiang's claim that Dante's theology is revolutionary because it dignifies imaginative reasoning inside sacred space.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's explanation for why Christianity's immense and unlikely global spread can be understood as more than a sociological accident.

chronology_notes.note: Jiang explicitly contrasts his 2026 classroom with the imagined constraints of the year 1300 to argue that Dante's questioning scene would have read as revolutionary in its own time.

uncertainty_notes.note: Jiang's rhetorical line about Jesus 'crucifying himself' is clearly loose speech rather than a doctrinal formulation, so preserve the larger point about Christianity's paradox rather than the exact phrasing as a literal claim.
